title: Clopen restriction of a supplied finite geometric categorical quotient
statement: Let $H$ be a finite group [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set] acting by automorphisms on a scheme $V$ [def-pc-scheme], and let $q:V\to X$ be an invariant finite surjective morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Assume that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ the map $V(\Omega)\to X(\Omega)$ is onto with fibres the $H$-orbits, that for every open $W\subseteq X$ the canonical map identifies $\mathcal O_X(W)$ with the $H$-invariant sections of $\mathcal O_V(q^{-1}W)$, and that every invariant morphism from $V$ to any scheme $T$ factors uniquely through $q$. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and closed, with its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $V_U=q^{-1}(U)$. Then $V_U$ is an open and closed $H$-invariant subscheme, with the induced action, and $q_U:V_U\to U$ is finite and surjective. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$, the map $V_U(\Omega)\to U(\Omega)$ is onto with fibres precisely the $H$-orbits. For every open $W\subseteq U$, the canonical map identifies $\mathcal O_U(W)$ with $\mathcal O_{V_U}(q_U^{-1}W)^H$. Every invariant morphism $V_U\to T$ to any scheme factors uniquely through $q_U$. If $q$ is an admissible finite scheme quotient [def-per-admissible-finite-scheme-quotient], then so is $q_U$. No field of definition, separatedness, finite-type, Noetherian or normality hypothesis is imposed on $V$ or $X$. The cases $U=\varnothing$ and $U=X$ are included.

proof.text: Put $C=X\setminus U$ and $D=q^{-1}(C)$, all subsets carrying their open subscheme structures. Continuity makes $V_U$ and $D$ complementary clopen subsets of $V$. Since $q\circ h=q$ for every $h\in H$, each action automorphism preserves both subsets. Restrict each automorphism using the unique factorization through an open subscheme; uniqueness preserves the identity, product and inverse laws. Similarly obtain $q_U$ and $q_C:D\to C$. The square with sides $V_U\to V$ and $U\to X$ is cartesian: any compatible pair of maps into $V$ and $U$ factors uniquely into $V_U$ by the open-factorization lemma. Finite base change (a) therefore makes $q_U$ finite. Every point of $U$ has a preimage under $q$, and that preimage lies in $V_U$, so $q_U$ is surjective.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field $\Omega$. Composition with the open inclusions identifies $U(\Omega)$ with the $\Omega$-points of $X$ landing in $U$, and $V_U(\Omega)$ with the $\Omega$-points of $V$ landing in $q^{-1}U$, by unique open factorization. A lift in $V(\Omega)$ of a point in $U(\Omega)$ necessarily lands in $q^{-1}U$, hence lifts to $V_U(\Omega)$. Two such lifts are in the same fibre exactly when their composites into $V$ are in the same fibre over $X$; the assumed orbit description supplies an $h\in H$ taking one to the other. Restriction of the action and uniqueness of open factorization give the same equality in $V_U(\Omega)$. Conversely invariance gives equality of their images.

source.place: Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens), applied to field-valued points; orbit-fibre hypothesis of the item

proof.text: An open $W\subseteq U$ is open in $X$, since $U$ is open. By the definition of the open subscheme structure, $\mathcal O_U(W)=\mathcal O_X(W)$ and $\mathcal O_{V_U}(q_U^{-1}W)=\mathcal O_V(q^{-1}W)$. Under these identifications the canonical ring map is the one assumed for $q$, and every action pullback is the same restriction of the original action pullback. The invariant subrings therefore agree as well. The assumed invariant-section identification for $q$ is exactly the required identification for $q_U$.

source.place: Tags 01HE and 01IO: structure sheaf of an open subscheme is the restricted sheaf

proof.text: Let $a:V_U\to T$ be any invariant morphism to any scheme $T$. Form $Y=T\amalg C$, with open coprojections $i_T,i_C$ having disjoint images covering $Y$. Glue $i_T\circ a$ on $V_U$ and $i_C\circ q_C$ on $D$ to a morphism $A:V\to Y$; their overlap is empty, so the compatibility condition is vacuous. For each $h\in H$, the maps $A\circ h$ and $A$ agree on $V_U$ by invariance of $a$ and on $D$ by invariance of $q_C$, so gluing uniqueness makes $A$ invariant. The supplied categorical quotient property of $q$ gives a unique $b:X\to Y$ with $b\circ q=A$.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue, first mapping property) and 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), for the two-piece disjoint union and gluing on complementary opens

proof.text: For each $u\in U$, choose $v\in V$ with $q(v)=u$. Then $v\in V_U$ and $b(u)=A(v)\in i_T(T)$. Consequently $b|_U$ factors uniquely through the open immersion $i_T$, giving $\bar a:U\to T$. Its composite with $q_U$ equals $a$: after composition with $i_T$ both morphisms are $A|_{V_U}$, and uniqueness of open factorization cancels $i_T$. This proves existence of the descent to $U$ without any assumption on $T$.

source.place: Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens); surjectivity hypothesis of the item

proof.text: If $a_1,a_2:U\to T$ satisfy $a_j\circ q_U=a$, glue $i_T\circ a_j$ on $U$ with $i_C\circ\mathrm{id}_C$ on $C$ to maps $b_j:X\to Y$. Each composite $b_j\circ q$ agrees with $A$ on $V_U$ and on $D$, hence equals $A$ by gluing uniqueness. Uniqueness in the supplied categorical quotient property gives $b_1=b_2$. Restriction to $U$ and uniqueness of factorization through $i_T$ give $a_1=a_2$. Thus every invariant $a$ descends uniquely.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue, mapping property) and 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens); categorical quotient hypothesis of the item

proof.text: Assume additionally that $q$ is admissible in the stated definition. Its underlying fibres are $H$-orbits, so the same holds for $q_U$ because $V_U$ is invariant. For a subset $E\subseteq U$, if $q_U^{-1}E$ is open in $V_U$, it is open in $V$ and equals $q^{-1}E$. The quotient-map property of $q$ makes $E$ open in $X$, hence in $U$; the converse follows by continuity. Thus $q_U$ is a topological quotient. For an orbit in $V_U$, let $u\in U$ be its image and choose an affine open $W\subseteq U$ containing $u$ using the affine-open basis. Then $q_U^{-1}W$ is an affine open containing the whole orbit: the map to $W$ is finite by finite base change (a) and its source is affine by (b). Together with finiteness, invariance and the invariant-section formula already proved, these are every clause of admissibility. All arguments allow $U=\varnothing$, $U=X$, and empty $V$ or $X$: gluing on empty overlaps is valid, and the pointwise assertions are vacuous when the relevant set is empty.

lean.statement: theorem clopen_geometric_categorical_quotient {H : Type v} [Group H] [Finite H] {V X : Scheme.{u}} (a : H →* Aut V) (q : V ⟶ X) [IsFinite q] [Surjective q] (hinv : ∀ h : H, (a h).hom ≫ q = q) (hpoints : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω], Function.Surjective (fun x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ V ↦ x ≫ q) ∧ ∀ x y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ V, x ≫ q = y ≫ q ↔ ∃ h : H, x ≫ (a h).hom = y) (hsections : ∀ W : X.Opens, Function.Injective (q.app W).hom ∧ ∀ s : Γ(V, q ⁻¹ᵁ W), (s ∈ Set.range (q.app W).hom ↔ ∀ (h : H) (O : V.Opens) (hO : O ≤ q ⁻¹ᵁ W) (hOh : O ≤ (a h).hom ⁻¹ᵁ (q ⁻¹ᵁ W)), ((a h).hom.appLE (q ⁻¹ᵁ W) O hOh).hom s = (V.presheaf.map (homOfLE hO).op).hom s)) (hcategorical : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : V ⟶ T), (∀ h : H, (a h).hom ≫ f = f) → ∃! g : X ⟶ T, q ≫ g = f) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsClopen (U : Set X)) : IsClopen (q ⁻¹ᵁ U : Set V) ∧ ∃ aU : H →* Aut (q ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme, (∀ h : H, (aU h).hom ≫ (q ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι = (q ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ≫ (a h).hom) ∧ IsFinite (morphismRestrict q U) ∧ Surjective (morphismRestrict q U) ∧ (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω], Function.Surjective (fun x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ (q ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme ↦ x ≫ morphismRestrict q U) ∧ ∀ x y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ (q ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme, x ≫ morphismRestrict q U = y ≫ morphismRestrict q U ↔ ∃ h : H, x ≫ (aU h).hom = y) ∧ (∀ W : U.toScheme.Opens, Function.Injective ((morphismRestrict q U).app W).hom ∧ ∀ s : Γ((q ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme, morphismRestrict q U ⁻¹ᵁ W), (s ∈ Set.range ((morphismRestrict q U).app W).hom ↔ ∀ (h : H) (O : (q ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.Opens) (hO : O ≤ morphismRestrict q U ⁻¹ᵁ W) (hOh : O ≤ (aU h).hom ⁻¹ᵁ (morphismRestrict q U ⁻¹ᵁ W)), ((aU h).hom.appLE (morphismRestrict q U ⁻¹ᵁ W) O hOh).hom s = ((q ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.presheaf.map (homOfLE hO).op).hom s)) ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : (q ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme ⟶ T), (∀ h : H, (aU h).hom ≫ f = f) → ∃! g : U.toScheme ⟶ T, morphismRestrict q U ≫ g = f) ∧ (IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient a q → IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient aU (morphismRestrict q U))
